+# notepad.exe (Windows 95, 4.00.950) — work in progress
+
+Target: `original/SYSTEM/notepad.exe` (34304 bytes, MD5 8198fd52174a2e347c20d5bd79e2af38).
+
+## Findings
+- PE32, LINK 2.50 / C 9.00 (Visual C++ 2.0), compiled with `/O1` (= /Ogsy, functions packed, no padding).
+- Headers and import libraries from the Win32 SDK (July 1995): `PAGESETUPDLG` exists there, and its
+  `commdlg.h` lacks `dllimport`, which is why COMDLG32 calls go through `jmp [IAT]` stubs.
+- `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` (or equivalent) is needed: VC2's `objbase.h` fails with C4226 otherwise.
+- Import hints come from import libraries of an earlier Win95 build (e.g. KERNEL32 LocalAlloc = 399, the
+  950 DLL has it at 400). They will need regenerated import libraries with matching export ordering.
+- Imports were bound (BIND.EXE) against the 950 retail DLLs in `original/SYSTEM/` (timestamps match),
+  and the PE checksum is set.
+- No C runtime: own entry point (`ModuleEntry`) at the start of `.text`.
+- Globals at 0x4053E0 are a `PAGESETUPDLG` (hDevMode +8, hDevNames +0xC, Flags 0xA006/0xA00A, margins).
+
+## Status (2026-10-15, session 2)
+A complete NOTEPAD.EXE now builds (`tools/build.sh notepad`) and runs; same size as the original
+(34304 bytes) with an identical section table.
+
+| Part | State |
+|---|---|
+| .data | identical (1024/1024) |
+| .bss | identical layout (npbss.asm + two file statics) |
+| .rsrc | identical except CVTRES timestamps |
+| .text | 27/57 functions byte-match |
+| .idata | same size; order follows code, hints need custom import libs |
+
+Per file: npmain.c 14/19, npinit.c 2/10, npsearch.c 0/2, npprint.c 2/10, strings.cpp 9/16.
+
+## Build settings found
+- `/Ogsy /Gz` (not `/O1`: that also pools identical strings, the original does not).
+- Full `<windows.h>` + `<commdlg.h> <cderr.h> <shellapi.h> <tchar.h>` (no WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN).
+- strings.cpp is compiled as C++ (register allocation only matches the C++ front end).
+- LINK 2.50: `/MERGE:.rdata=.text /SECTION:.idata,R`, objects in .text order, npbss.obj last.
+- Resource statements in the original .rc order (icons, menu, accelerators, dialogs, version,
+  string blocks 4,3,1,2).
+- "intl" literal: a dead `if (0)` branch in NpWinIniChange keeps the string (original had dead code).
+- .bss: LINK 2.50 allocates commons in reverse object order and, within an object, in the
+  compiler's symbol-hash order of the (unknown) original names, so npbss.asm fixes the layout.
+
+## Next steps
+1. Custom import-library generator (undecorated import names, original hint values); BIND; set
+   build timestamps (PE header 0x2FF3548D, resource dirs 0x2FF3548C); checksum.
+2. Keep tuning functions in file order (npinit, npsearch, npprint are still first drafts).
+
+## Important: codegen depends on everything before it in the file
+CL 9.x breaks register/operand-order ties using state that depends on all symbols seen so far
+(headers, earlier functions, declarations).  Padding experiments show it is chaotic, not a simple
+count.  Header choice alone moved npmain from 11 to 14 matches.  CL 9.x carries per-file state between functions: changing an earlier function can change register
+choice / compare operand order in later ones (NPWndProc, MergeStrings flipped when only NPCommand
+changed). Match functions strictly in file order; re-check the whole file after every edit.
+Open issues: InitPageSetupDefaults (branch tails merged), NPCommand paste compare (2 bytes),
+PFileInPath / WinMain / GetFileName / NPInitStrings register allocation, NPRegister store order.
+
+Source-level lessons that fixed mismatches: declaration order, `MAKEPOINTS` (takes &lParam),
+signed `int` switch variables, WORD-typed globals, two `++` instead of `+= 2`, case order (jump table
+reveals source order), `switch` with separate calls instead of `?:` arguments, a case label inside an
+`if` block (M_EXIT shares Open's PostMessage).
+
+## Tools
+- `tools/cc32.sh` – compile with CL 9.00 + SDK headers (writes .obj and .cod)
+- `tools/coffcmp.py <obj> original/SYSTEM/notepad.exe src/notepad/symbols.txt -v` – per-function compare
+- `tools/ghidra/decompile.sh` – Ghidra headless first-draft decompilation
+- `tools/res2rc.py` – PE resources -> RC script (work in progress); `tools/peres.py`, `tools/peinfo.py`
+- `tools/fdiff.py <obj> original/SYSTEM/notepad.exe src/notepad/symbols.txt <func>` – side-by-side diff
+- `tools/dis.py original/SYSTEM/notepad.exe src/notepad/symbols.txt src/notepad/data.txt <func>` –
+  original disassembly annotated with our symbol names
+
+## Symbol-count padding (nppad.h)
+
+CL 9.00 breaks register-allocation and operand-order ties using its internal
+symbol numbering, which depends on how many symbols were declared before each
+function (it repeats every 32 symbols). The original was built with internal
+Win95 headers that we don't have, so each source file defines
+`NPPAD` (0-31) and includes `nppad.h`, which declares that many unused
+externs. Offsets were found by scanning (`PADS=0-31 tools/variants.py ...`):
+npmain 31, npinit 20, npsearch 12, npprint 21, strings 11. This alone fixed
+InitPageSetupDefaults, PrintFileCheck and InsertDateTime, and two strings
+functions.

+# NOTEPAD.EXE (32-bit) -- sourced by tools/build.sh (helpers in tools/buildlib.sh)
+CFLAGS="/Ogsy /Gz /W3"
+for f in npmain.c npinit.c npsearch.c npprint.c strings.cpp; do
+    cc32 "$SRC/$f" $CFLAGS "/I$(winpath "$SRC")"
+done
+uasm -q -coff -Cp -Fonpbss.obj "$SRC/npbss.asm"
+python3 "$ROOT/tools/peicons.py" "$ROOT/original/SYSTEM/notepad.exe" . >/dev/null
+rc32 "$SRC/notepad.rc"
+
+# Import libraries: the Win32 SDK libraries with the hint values of the
+# (earlier Windows 95 build) libraries the original was linked against.
+LIBS="SHELL32 KERNEL32 USER32 GDI32 COMDLG32"
+for l in $LIBS; do
+    python3 "$ROOT/tools/patchhints.py" "$ROOT/win32sdk/LIB/I386/$l.LIB" "$l.LIB" \
+        "$ROOT/original/SYSTEM/notepad.exe" >/dev/null
+done
+
+link32 notepad.exe /NODEFAULTLIB /ENTRY:ModuleEntry@0 /SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS,4.0 \
+    /MERGE:.rdata=.text /SECTION:.idata,R \
+    npmain.obj npinit.obj npsearch.obj npprint.obj strings.obj npbss.obj notepad.rbj \
+    SHELL32.LIB KERNEL32.LIB USER32.LIB GDI32.LIB COMDLG32.LIB
+
+# Post-link, as in the original build: build timestamps (link and CVTRES
+# run times), bind imports against the Windows 95 (950) DLLs, checksum.
+python3 "$ROOT/tools/pestamp.py" notepad.exe 2ff3548d 2ff3548c
+mkdir -p binddll
+for l in shell32 kernel32 user32 gdi32 comdlg32; do
+    cp "$ROOT/original/SYSTEM/$l.dll" "binddll/$l.dll"
+done
+# BIND needs the real IMAGEHLP.DLL (Wine's built-in BindImageEx is a stub);
+# IMAGEHLP is a "known DLL" in Wine, so drop that entry in our private prefix.
+wine reg delete 'HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\KnownDLLs' \
+    /v imagehlp /f </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+cp "$ROOT/rc4/BIND.EXE" "$ROOT/rc4/IMAGEHLP.DLL" .
+WINEDLLOVERRIDES="$WINEDLLOVERRIDES;imagehlp=n" wine ./BIND.EXE -o -u -p binddll notepad.exe \
+    </dev/null 2>&1 | tr -d '\r' | grep -v '^$' || true
+python3 "$ROOT/tools/pechecksum.py" notepad.exe
+
+compare32 notepad.exe SYSTEM/notepad.exe

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compare functions in a COFF .obj (VC++ 2.0) with an original PE image.
+
+Usage: coffcmp.py <file.obj> <orig.exe> <symbols.txt> [-v] [-q]
+symbols.txt: "<hex VA> <name>" per line (undecorated C name; '#' comments).
+Bytes covered by relocations in the .obj are masked.  Each function is
+matched by name against symbols.txt; -v prints mismatching byte ranges with
+disassembly hints, -q prints only the summary line."""
+import sys, struct
+objf, exe, symf = sys.argv[1:4]; verbose = '-v' in sys.argv; quiet = '-q' in sys.argv
+o = open(objf, 'rb').read(); d = open(exe, 'rb').read()
+# --- PE
+pe = struct.unpack_from('<I', d, 0x3c)[0]; nsec = struct.unpack_from('<H', d, pe+6)[0]
+osz = struct.unpack_from('<H', d, pe+20)[0]; base = struct.unpack_from('<I', d, pe+52)[0]
+psecs = [struct.unpack_from('<IIII', d, pe+24+osz+40*i+8) for i in range(nsec)]
+def va2off(va):
+    rva = va - base
+    for vs, sva, rs, ro in psecs:
+        if sva <= rva < sva + rs: return rva - sva + ro
+syms = {}
+for line in open(symf):
+    f = line.split('#')[0].split()
+    if len(f) >= 2: syms[f[1]] = int(f[0], 16)
+# --- COFF
+mach, ns, ts, symptr, nsym, ohsz, ch = struct.unpack_from('<HHIIIHH', o, 0)
+secs = []
+for i in range(ns):
+    p = 20 + ohsz + 40*i
+    name = o[p:p+8].rstrip(b'\0').decode('latin-1')
+    vs, va, rs, rp, relp, lnp, nrel, nln, sch = struct.unpack_from('<IIIIIIHHI', o, p+8)
+    data = o[rp:rp+rs]; mask = bytearray(rs)
+    for r in range(nrel):
+        roff, rsym, rtype = struct.unpack_from('<IIH', o, relp+10*r)
+        n = 4 if rtype in (6, 7, 0x14) else 2
+        for k in range(n): mask[roff+k] = 1
+    secs.append((name, data, mask, sch))
+strtab = symptr + 18*nsym
+def symname(p):
+    if o[p:p+4] == b'\0\0\0\0':
+        so = strtab + struct.unpack_from('<I', o, p+4)[0]; return o[so:o.index(b'\0', so)].decode()
+    return o[p:p+8].rstrip(b'\0').decode('latin-1')
+funcs = []; i = 0
+while i < nsym:
+    p = symptr + 18*i
+    val, sec, typ, cls, naux = struct.unpack_from('<IhHBB', o, p+8)
+    nm = symname(p)
+    if sec > 0 and (typ & 0x30) == 0x20 and cls in (2, 3):    # function symbol
+        funcs.append((nm, sec-1, val))
+    i += 1 + naux
+def undecorate(n):
+    n = n[1:] if n[:1] in '_@?' else n
+    return n.split('@')[0]
+total = good = 0
+for nm, si, val in funcs:
+    sname, data, mask, sch = secs[si]
+    # function extent: up to next function in same section or section end
+    ends = sorted(v for n2, s2, v in funcs if s2 == si and v > val)
+    end = ends[0] if ends else len(data)
+    cname = undecorate(nm)
+    if cname not in syms:
+        if not quiet: print('%-28s (no address in symbols file)' % cname)
+        continue
+    po = va2off(syms[cname]); orig = d[po:po + end - val]
+    diffs = [k for k in range(end - val) if not mask[val+k] and data[val+k] != orig[k]]
+    total += 1; good += not diffs
+    if not quiet:
+        print('%-28s %08x %5d bytes  %s' % (cname, syms[cname], end - val,
+              'MATCH' if not diffs else '%d bytes differ (first at +%#x)' % (len(diffs), diffs[0])))
+    if verbose and diffs:
+        k0 = max(0, diffs[0] - 8)

latest_release.body:
Second tagged build of the standalone game.

Level 1 now plays from the intro cutscene into gameplay, and you can move
Spider-Man with the keyboard. Sound, music and the movies are still stubs.
Expect bugs.

Fixed since v0.0.1 (every fix checked against the original game running
under Wine):

- The arrow keys move Spider-Man. The player code cleared all pad buttons
  every frame, so no key press ever reached him.
- The mouse is not inverted any more. The two axes were swapped.
- Black Cat shows up in her scene. Her aim was mirrored, so she walked away
  from Spider-Man, and the shadow code overwrote her body matrix, so she was
  drawn lying flat on the roof.
- The difficulty menu has its box and the little Spider-Man again.
- The window opens at 2x (1280x960). Set SPIDEY_SCALE=1 for the old size.
- The HUD is not sheared any more (health bar, compass needle and arrow).
- Menu and viewer models do not explode any more (anim decoder with a block
  size of 1).

latest_release.body:
Fix release on top of sc3mods-2026-10-11. Same five mods and launcher. Only `sc3resize.dll` and `mods_launch.exe` changed, the other four DLLs are the same files.

**Fixed**
- Main menu when the window is bigger than 800x600: the 2026-10-11 build stretched the whole menu, buttons included, and clicks landed on the wrong button. Now the menu fills the window with the included `menu_bg.bmp` and the buttons stay at normal size, centered, where you click them.
- Maximizing a 1024 city no longer freezes for 2 to 3 s. The mod's resize work went from about 2.2 s to 0.15 s.
- The crash about 1 second after maximizing, in the terrain drawing, is fixed at its cause: the screen was split into dirty-rectangle cells rounded down, so the last rows got drawn past the end of the screen buffer.
- One loading box instead of two when you load or start a city while maximized.
- Dialogs re-center correctly after maximize and restore.
- P and 1 to 4 do nothing while you type in a text box (city name, save name).

**New file**
- `menu_bg.bmp`: an upscaled main menu picture. Replace it with any 24-bit uncompressed BMP to use your own. Delete it to get the stock picture stretched to the window.

**Install**
Unzip everything you want into the game's `Apps` folder, next to `SC3U.exe`, replacing the 2026-10-11 files, and start the game with `mods_launch.exe`.

**Known limits**
- Resizing while the simulation is in the middle of a heavy step waits for that step to finish (seen once at 3.4 s on a 1024 city). That wait is what stops the resize from crashing into a half-updated city.
- White or frozen picture after maximizing: copy `SC3U.exe` to `SC3U_mods.exe` and start with `mods_launch.exe -exe SC3U_mods.exe`.
- Changing your monitor setup while the game runs can crash it. That's DirectDraw, not the mods.
